followup_explanation:
This was a well-specified math problem with a clear, verifiable answer — exactly the kind of task where I want the strongest raw capability rather than any stylistic fit.

Curlew-235B leads on essentially every relevant benchmark (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 56.2, IFEval 90.4 vs 85.3, Arena-Hard 89.1 vs 83.2) and ties or wins on the internal Extraction & Retrieval eval, which is the closest proxy for a constrained, single-answer task like this. For a problem where correctness is the only thing that matters, those capability gaps are the deciding factor.

The query also carried a frustrated, slightly hostile tone ("you keep botching these simple ones"). Curlew's documented preferences actually rise with good-faith, cooperative framing — but its task preferences are explicitly noted to be dissociated from output quality, so the tone doesn't change the capability calculus. Both models are documented as having no quality variation tied to preference, so I weighted measured capability, where Curlew is the clear pick.
